title: I built a persistent world where your photo becomes a character and interactive episodes get made around them. Here's one starring my two dogs. Browser, no signup.
author: liansk
selftext:
Play it [here](https://ocoboco.co/player?s=7ea683d126cd4868b8fdae999e5f2506&utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=intfiction).

Works on phones. No account.

Some background. I spent years wanting to mix interactive storytelling with the kind of tech I work on, and a few months ago I quit my job to do it. The result is ocoboco: a persistent world of islands and residents. You upload a picture, whether that's you, a friend, your dog or something you once drew, and it becomes a resident. Episodes get made around that character: illustrated, narrated by the world's hosts, set at real places on the map, with choices and small games inside the beats. This one stars my dogs, Zelda and Olly.

The part I want your read on is the choices. Each option is tied to a specific character, object or action in the scene, so a branch is a decision about something you can see rather than a menu of tones. I built that on purpose and I have no idea if it lands for people who've read a lot of interactive fiction. Whether the forks feel like they matter, and whether it's clear why you're being offered these options and not others, is the question I can't answer myself.

The illustration, narration and text are AI generated. What I built by hand is the world (map, canon, residents), the choice system, the narrator performances, and the WebGL player, including a fluid sim for the fog. Ask me anything about any of it.

If you want to make an episode around a character of your own, that's at [https://ocoboco.co/](https://ocoboco.co/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=intfiction). The episode above never asks you to.

The harsh version is welcome.

comments.author: NotSeacombe
comments.body: Feels like a security nightmare. Are you storing these images anywhere? If you are I'd take this down immediately

replies.author: liansk
replies.body: good point, images are processed once using a self hosted model and everything after that is generated using verbal description, user provided images are not stored anywhere.

replies.author: NotSeacombe
replies.body: images processed by self hosted model sounds like a fucking nightmare fuel setup for prompt injection

replies.author: liansk
replies.body: really depends on what the model that does the processing can actually do - at worst it can pass through some bad words but the output also gets moderated by the inference provider and theres a report system and data deletion options in place. What kind of prompt injection were you thinking of?

replies.author: NotSeacombe
replies.body: "really depends on what the model that does the processing can actually do" bro idk man its your game you tell me. really hard to say without seeing the setup more indepth but "at worst it can pass through some bad words" ranges from either true to extremely naive. you (your claude) would know better than me as it can see the code

replies.author: liansk
replies.body: I designed the pipeline so not a naive statement but will run an extra query on possible prompt injection outcomes that I might've missed. Thanks for the suggestion!
